title: Store ownership: one deep .mulch store module (lenient | strict | raw-line policies, compact rewrite)
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 1, Strong). Evidence: the lib `Store` has ZERO callers in the binary; six readers and five writers implement the same file conventions independently (commands/mod.rs raw-line IO, status/validate/doctor lenient reads, records.rs strict reader/writer, ConfigStore writing mulch.config.yaml itself). Problem: the format contract lives in prose + duplicated IO; every one of the ~20 remaining parity commands needs another read+write of the same store. Solution: name the access policies (lenient | strict | raw-line for reads; rewrite-compact | append-verbatim for writes) in the lib store module and move the CLI's file IO behind them, starting with one pilot command (status). Benefits: locality (the reference semantics live in one place), leverage (each new command inherits the policies), tests (policy-level unit tests replace per-command store fixtures). Note: README DEVIATIONS pins the lenient/strict reader split as CONTRACT — the deepening must name both policies, never merge them. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html (temp, ephemeral).

[2026-10-03, local iterate loop] Sprint 4 pick (of the five arch-gate candidates + three remaining parity slices): the user said 'weiter' without naming one, so priority order decides — this is a Strong candidate and the gate's top recommendation, and it makes the remaining ~20 parity commands cheaper; the alternative Strong candidate (mulch-9e70, command boundary) is deliberately SECOND so it can reuse the seam this sprint creates.
closeReason: Store ownership landed (commits vwm + rlu): lib StoreFiles owns discovery (StoreLocation), config mutations (register/remove/delete domain, canonical write) and the explicit read/write policies (read_records strict with the allow-unknown escape hatch, read_lines for the reporting commands, rewrite_domain compact+id-generation, append_domain_line verbatim); ConfigStore and the CLI IO helpers deleted; the locate->message+channel policy has one owner (open_store); status/validate/doctor read through the seam; edit/outcome/record read strictly before any write. title: record upsert semantics: named-type duplicates update in place (not an anonymous advisory)
description:
Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind; pre-existing since mulch-fdd0). Reference `commands/record.ts:1085-1130`: a duplicate on pattern/decision/reference/guide UPSERTS in place and prints `✓ Updated existing <type> in <domain> (record #N)`; the batch path reports `updated` in its counters. Ours always prints `Duplicate <type> already exists in <domain> (record #N). Use --force to add anyway.` and writes nothing; batch counts it as `skipped`. Also: the dedupe key is wrong — the reference `findDuplicate` (utils/expertise.ts:194-217) compares the TYPE'S DEDUP FIELD, ours compares the id, so a store holding a renamed record (which `edit --name` produces, since neither side recomputes ids) gets a second appended record where the reference upserts one. Evidence: 3-way probes in the sprint-4 spec review (/tmp/review, report lines 2-3).

SPRINT 6 PICK (2026-10-04): bug before features — same data-integrity class as mulch-b88b (wrong store shape on the write path: duplicate append where the reference upserts one record, plus the wrong dedupe key compounds after edit --name renames). 351d/ca49/9e70 follow.

title: doctor: our `duplicates` check is a hardcoded pass — the reference reports `N duplicate record(s) found` with per-record details on the same store

- summary: `! 1 duplicate record(s) found` (warn status; count = number of REDUNDANT records, not of ids);
